programs.name: pause
programs.purpose: Print a prompt and wait for a character from standard input.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: PAUSE - prompt and wait for user signal to continue
programs.float_sensitive_notes: Concatenating sufficiently long command-line arguments overflows the fixed-size do_what buffer, causing undefined behavior.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program builds a prompt from positional arguments and reads one character.

test_cases.description: Use the default prompt and provide a newline.
Use multiple positional words in the prompt.

programs.name: t
programs.purpose: Print the current local time and date in a 12-hour style.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: T - time and date for non-military types
programs.float_sensitive_notes: Output depends on the current clock and local time zone, so it is not a stable golden without controlling time; midnight is printed as hour 0.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program formats the current local date and time without numerical processing.

test_cases.description: Print the date and time in UTC.
Print the date and time in a different local time zone.

programs.name: upfort
programs.purpose: Convert Fortran source to uppercase while preserving comments and most quoted strings.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: UPFORT - change Fortran programs to upper case, preserving strings
programs.float_sensitive_notes: The inner loops do not check for EOF, so a final line without a newline or an unterminated quoted string can cause an infinite loop; character classification also depends on the C locale.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program transforms characters in a single input stream with simple comment and quote handling.

test_cases.description: Convert code while preserving a comment and a quoted string.
test_cases.command:
printf 'c mixed Case comment
      print *, '''Mixed Case'''
      end
' | upfort

test_cases.description: Exercise the special quoted text beginning with an opening parenthesis.
